newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Funds row forces U.S. lawyers out of U.N. tribunal.
newsitem.headline: Funds row forces U.S. lawyers out of U.N. tribunal.

text.p: Sixteen U.S. legal staff attached to the Yugoslav war crimes tribunal in The Hague will have to leave because of a financial dispute between the United States and the United Nations, the tribunal said on Friday.
The lawyers and investigators are paid by the United States, but U.N. rules specify an additional payment, equivalent to 13 percent of their salaries, to defray the tribunal's fixed costs.

"It's not a pleasant situation and it's something we deplore very much," said tribunal spokesman Christian Chartier, adding: "It is really over a very small amount of money and is obviously part of a more general dispute," he said.
The United States is currently witholding U.N. dues and other payments worth over $1.3 billion, making it the organisation's biggest debtor.
The U.S. personnel form part of a team of 34 legal professionals from 11 countries working to investigate and prosecute war crimes committed during the Bosnian conflict.
Ten of the Americans will leave in six weeks time while six, who are involved in cases at a critical stage, will postpone their departure for three months, Chartier said.
The tribunal, set up by the U.N. Security Council in 1993, has indicted over 70 Serbs, Croats and Moslems with war crimes, but holds only seven suspects in its custody.
